newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany still opposes IMF gold sales.
newsitem.headline: Germany still opposes IMF gold sales.

text.p: Germany remains opposed to gold sales by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), finance state secretary Juergen Stark said in a newspaper interview on Wednesday.
Ahead of the IMF's annual meeting this week, Stark told the Handelsblatt that Germany wished to avoid an open dispute over the IMF's proposals to sell gold to aid the world's poorest countries.
Germany has alternative financing plans to offer that would make gold sales unnecessary, he said.

The two other main messages it wishes to get across are that Germany -- unlike some other important donor countries -- is up to date in its global payments, and that reform and restructuring in Germany is proceeding apace.
Germany is also interested in briefing its partners, particularly the U.S., on the expected impact of the future single European currency, the Euro, on world foreign exchange markets, Stark said.
"There is a great deal to explain. There is a general uneasiness, particularly on the American side," Stark said.
Germany remains optimistic about the situation in Russia despite the serious illness of President Boris Yeltsin, Stark said.
